name: Vanthorpe Meridian Wrist Locus MK-2
description:
A flat-profile smart-watch in brushed titanium with a single curved sapphire-analog display face that renders digital data as moving hands and analog dials — a deliberate aesthetic choice that reads as retro confidence rather than nostalgia. Case width is 42mm; the strap is a double-deployant clasp band in midnight-navy Uruguayan calf leather with a micro-perforated inner face.

The bezel rotates mechanically but also registers haptic input, syncing with BCI overlays to surface calendar, biometric, and comms data without visible screens.
functionality: BCI-synced haptic bezel delivers silent notifications and data overlays. Analog face masks smart functions from casual observation — security through aesthetics. Biometric monitoring includes cortisol, pulse, and blood-oxygen. 72-hour charge cycle via kinetic harvesting.
what_it_says: You have enough money to look like you don't need to prove it.
story_hooks: The MK-2 had a firmware vulnerability patched in the third production run — earlier units can be silently read by anyone with the right scanner.
A Tier-5 broker is known to judge every meeting by whether the other party wears analog or digital — the Locus MK-2 is the only watch that passes either test.
Someone returned a Locus MK-2 to a Circuit pawn shop with the biometric log wiped but the calendar still intact.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sophisticated minimalist timepiece that reads as analog luxury despite its digital core. The brushed titanium case sits flush against the wrist with intentional restraint, projecting quiet confidence and technical expertise. The curved sapphire face creates a gentle lens effect that catches light like a traditional mechanical watch, contradicting its neural interface capabilities.
physical_description.fit: Snug and secure against the wrist. The double-deployant clasp provides adjustable fit without visible fasteners, sitting flush to the skin. The micro-perforated leather inner face allows subtle ventilation for extended wear, even with dermal augmentation interfaces.
physical_description.primary_material: Brushed titanium case; midnight-navy Uruguayan calf leather strap with micro-perforated backing; sapphire crystal curved display face
physical_description.texture: The titanium bezel has a soft, non-reflective matte finish. The sapphire lens is perfectly smooth with a slight convex curve. The leather strap is supple yet structured, with visible micro-perforations creating a subtle tactile pattern on the inner face.
physical_description.color_scheme: Titanium silver-grey case with midnight-navy leather strap. The analog hand mechanisms (hours, minutes, auxiliary dials) feature subtle accent colors—likely silver or deep bronze—visible through the sapphire face against a dark dial backdrop.
physical_description.closures: Double-deployant clasp mechanism in matching titanium; no visible latches or fasteners. Designed for one-handed adjustment.
distinctive_features: Rotating mechanical bezel with haptic input registration
Sapphire-analog hybrid display rendering digital data as moving hands and rotating dials
Micro-perforated leather backing suggests advanced moisture/heat management
BCI sync capability integrated into bezel rotation—no visible tech signatures
Curved sapphire lens creates vintage watchmaker aesthetic masking cutting-edge neural interface
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 1-2 luxury. The Vanthorpe brand, Uruguayan leather sourcing, and titanium construction signal high-tier corporate or independent wealth. Price point likely 8,000-15,000 Φ.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by corpo executives, independent ops, and augmented professionals who reject visible tech displays as status signaling. The retro-analog aesthetic appeals to those who view cutting-edge functionality as something that should whisper, not shout. Suggests neural interface access without the cyberpunk cliché of holographic projections.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine or carefully maintained with minor patina. The leather may show subtle wear at the clasp after extended use, but the titanium and sapphire resist visible degradation. Owners typically maintain these as signature pieces, not disposable accessories.
